# External Sources: One Place, One Vocabulary

How data from other sites (start.gg, smash-tube.com, ultimateframedata.com, ...) enters the library, so that
functions built on different sites can be combined without translating between them.

## Rules

1. **All external sourcing lives under `pkgs/ds/data/`.** Code that calls another site or API goes in
   `pkgs/ds/data/raw/<site>.py` (or `raw/<site>/` when it is large). Nothing outside `ds/data` makes requests
   to a data source: `ds/ai`, `ds/calc`, `tools/` and scripts call `ds.data` functions.
2. **Outputs are normalized at that boundary.** A public function in `ds.data` speaks this repo's vocabulary,
   not the site's. Callers never see or pass a site's own ids.
3. **Public functions take the normalized values as input too.** A character argument is a `char_id` (or a `char_group` where the data is about picks)
   (eg `little_mac`), never a site's name or id. The site module translates on the way out.

## The vocabulary

| Thing | Standard | Source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| Character (a fighter) | `char_id`, eg `little_mac`, `pt_squirtle` | `char.parquet` (`id`) |
| Character (a pick) | `char_group`, eg `little_mac`, `pokemon_trainer` | `char.parquet` (`char_group`), `ds.data.CHAR_GROUPS` |
| Character icon | `char_icon`, a path under `pkgs/ds/data/` | `char.parquet` (`char_icon`), `ds.data.char_icon` |
| Foreign key column / field | `{table}_id` | `.agents/instructions/pkgs.md`, "`ds/data` Conventions" |
| Time | timezone-aware UTC `datetime`; `date` for day-only values | |
| Field names | snake_case, the same word for the same thing across sites (`tag`, `online`, `start_at`) | |
| Tables | `polars.DataFrame` | `spec/pkgs/dataframes.md` |
| Fixed-shape records | pydantic models with `Field(description=...)` | |

Stages have no table yet. Until one exists, sites return their own stage names (see "Open points").

## Characters: how a site's name becomes a `char_id`

Every site names characters its own way (display names with different punctuation, Japanese names, numeric
ids, icon file names). The translation belongs to the site's module and is the main thing this spec is about.

- **Match by display name first:** `ds.data.char_id_by_name(name)` (a fighter), `ds.data.char_group_by_name(name)`
  (a pick) and `ds.data.char_icon_by_name(name)`
  ignore case, punctuation and `&` / `and` (`Banjo-Kazooie`, `Banjo & Kazooie` -> `banjo_and_kazooie`).
- **Use an explicit map when names can't match** (another language, the site's own slugs), keyed by `char_id`
  and kept in the site module, eg `SITE_CHARACTER` in `raw/smashtube.py`, `SITE_CHAR_ICON` in
  `raw/smashmate.py`. A test checks the map covers every `char.parquet` id.
- **Keep the site's value next to the normalized one** when it is needed to call the site again or to debug
  (eg start.gg's numeric character `id` beside `char_group`). It is extra, never the key callers use.
- **Fighters and picks.** A `char.parquet` row is a *fighter* (its own moves and frame data). A *pick* is a
  character-select entry. They differ for two picks: `pokemon_trainer` (`pt_squirtle`, `pt_ivysaur`,
  `pt_charizard`) and `pyra_mythra` (`pyra`, `mythra`). Frame-data sites list fighters (ultimateframedata.com
  has no Pokemon Trainer page); tournament sites record picks (start.gg doesn't say which Pokemon was out).
  - **`char.parquet` has both:** `id` is the fighter, `char_group` the pick it belongs to (its own id when
    it isn't grouped). Decided Nov 2026, after trying one member as a stand-in: that made a join to frame
    data return only that member's moves.
  - **A source that knows fighters returns `char_id`; one that only knows picks returns `char_group`.**
    Don't put a group id in a `char_id` field or a fighter in place of a pick.
  - **Joining a pick to fighters:** on `char_group`, which gives every member (`ds.data.char_group_members`).
  - **Inputs:** a function about picks accepts a fighter id, a group id or a name and narrows it with
    `ds.data.char_group_by_name` (`pt_ivysaur` -> `pokemon_trainer`).
  - **Our id -> site (input to a site with one entry per pick):** every member maps to the site's one value.
- **No match is `None`, not an error and not the raw name in the id field** (eg "Random"). Site
  modules should make unmatched names easy to list (the start.gg probe prints them).

## Where each source stands

| Source | Module | Characters | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| ultimateframedata.com | `raw/framedata.py`, `raw/roster.py` | site slug is the origin of `char.parquet` ids | normalized (defines the standard) |
| nasmashmate.com (icons) | `raw/smashmate.py` | `SITE_CHAR_ICON`: `char_id` -> site icon name | normalized |
| smash-tube.com | `raw/smashtube.py` | `SITE_CHARACTER`: `char_id` -> Japanese name; inputs are `char_id` | normalized on input |
| start.gg | `raw/startgg/` | name match; `Character.char_group` + `char_icon`, site `id` kept | normalized (picks, so `char_group`) |
| supermajor.gg | `raw/supermajor.py` | returns the site's ids (`A1297`) and names | **not normalized** (TODO in file); player pages blocked since Nov 2026, so left as is |

## Layers inside a large source

A source big enough to be a package (`raw/startgg/`) keeps two layers apart:

- `ds/data/raw/<site>/`: the site as it is. One function per request, normalization only.
- `ds/data/<site>/`: what we compute from it (aggregates, joins with other sources, derived stats).

Both layers return the normalized vocabulary; the split is about how much is computed, not about naming.

## Keeping sources current

- Code written from a site's documentation carries `# ds::external-source:` tags; the `external-review` skill
  (`.agents/skills/external-review/SKILL.md`) re-reads those pages.
- Scrapers of undocumented pages keep a "Site notes" header (findings, decisions, dead ends).

## Open points

- **Stages:** no `stage` table, so no `stage_id`. Stage names differ per site (`Pokémon Stadium 2` vs
  `Pokemon Stadium 2`, `PS2`). Needed once stage usage from start.gg is combined with anything else.
- **Players:** no shared player id across sites. start.gg's player id is the natural key (supermajor's
  `S<digits>` looks like the same number); tags are not unique.
